findings.issue: The structural scan (result_scan, sc-ua10/sc-ua11) can be fooled by a reader that hands the narrowed list to a helper, and the comment claims more than it delivers. Taint is only set by `x = R["during"]` (a direct Subscript, line 300-303); an assignment from a call (`during = _drop_config(strays["during"])`, or `during = _drop_config(during)` after the tainted assignment) taints nothing, and a Call argument is never examined, so nothing is flagged. The helper itself is not scanned either: only functions that call `undeclared_changes` are walked (line 268), so a comprehension over its parameter is invisible. Passing the WHOLE answer to a helper is caught (`used other than by key`), but passing a list read by key is not. Further holes in the same shape: a `for p in R["during"]` loop that appends in an else branch rather than using `continue` (325-329); `_only_membership` accepts any comparator that is not a literal and not an upper-case Name, so `p not in _skiplist()`, `p in _mio.SKIP` (Attribute) and a lower-case module list all count as 'computed' (251-253); a tuple-unpacked or `or`-wrapped read is not tainted. The comment at 207-217 says the lists may be narrowed 'by a membership test ... and by nothing else' and that a reader has 'no way to rebuild it ... handing it on' - false for the helper route. The docstring at _scoped_commit.py:~1160 does admit 'a reader that reaches a skip by a route neither describes is not caught', which satisfies the first alternative of P137-R2, but the helper hand-off is the most obvious such route and is cheap to close. Read from the code; not run.
findings.resolution: Make taint transitive: an Assign whose value contains any tainted name or a by-key read of an UNDECLARED_KEYS list taints its targets (any expression, including calls, BoolOps, tuples). Flag a tainted value passed as an argument to any call except a short allowlist of presentation builtins (len, sorted, set, list, tuple, str.join) and, for a same-file helper receiving it, scan that helper's body with its parameter as tainted. Narrow `_only_membership` to a comparator that is a bare lower-case Name bound in the function from something other than a literal, and flag loops that filter without `continue` (any `if` guarding an append of the loop variable). Add a sc-ua11 mutation per hole (call-wrapped, helper, Attribute comparator). Or reword the comment so it does not say 'nothing else'.

findings.issue: `_is_tracked` returns True when git cannot answer, which is the loud direction for the commit and the close (the config counts as an undeclared change and the verb refuses; nothing is written) but the unsafe one for the set-aside. There `plugin_owned_rels` is read as a PROTECTION list (`plugin_owned_paths` -> `settle_aside`: 'Nothing is reverted ... when one of paths is plugin-owned'). A config wrongly judged tracked is not in that list, so it is reverted by `git checkout HEAD` or, when HEAD does not hold it, deleted by `os.remove` (drive-phase.py:3685-3691). Reaching that needs `ls-files` to fail (or `plan_to_git` to return None) while `ls-tree` and `checkout` succeed, so it is narrow, and the patch keeps the bytes; but one function now serves three readers with opposite safe directions and the diff chose the direction by the two that refuse. `plan_to_git` None (outside the checkout) is also read as tracked, though nothing outside the checkout is listed by status in the first place. Judgement from reading; sc-ua9's `blind_rows` pins only the 'not exempted' side and no case pins the set-aside side of a failed answer.
findings.resolution: Return a tri-state from `_is_tracked` (tracked / untracked / unknown) and let `plugin_owned_rels` place the config for the refusing readers when unknown, while `plugin_owned_paths` treats unknown as owned (protected), or have set_aside refuse to revert a path whose tracked state is unknown. Add a case with git unavailable for the set-aside reader.

findings.issue: The change edits tests/test_drive_phase.py, which is in neither the task's `files` nor its `tests.gate` (the gate is the three suites test__scoped_commit, test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work). The behaviour change really does turn xs6 red (a tracked config is no longer plugin-owned for the set-aside), so the recorded gate run, which passed, would have passed over a stale xs6; only the executor's own wider gate command ran it. The brief's diff also omits the file, so a reader of the brief does not see the set-aside's new expectation. The outcome does describe the xs6 change, so the claim is honest; the scope declaration is not.
findings.resolution: Add tests/test_drive_phase.py to the task's files and to tests.gate (retarget --gate-set) so the dependant suite is part of the recorded gate, or record the widening as a scope note on the task.
